items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are clear (`buildWindowSpec`, `unboundedPreceding`, the `rank` ordering field), but none of the new public helpers have docstrings, unlike existing builder methods. `rows()`/`range()` are near-identical blocks, and storing windows as tuples (`windows.map(([name, spec]) =>`) hides what each element means.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The same `.window()` validation (`'Window name must be a non-empty string'`, whitespace check) is copied into all 5 dialect builders instead of one shared assert. `rows()` and `range()` duplicate their validation and SQL building. The file is in `sql/expressions/` rather than the `sql/functions` location the conventions asked for.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Inputs are checked at the boundary: `preceding`/`following` reject negative and non-integer offsets and name the helper; the from/to order check uses the rank values; window names are type-, empty- and whitespace-checked. Numbers are inlined via `sql.raw(String(offset))`, never bound as parameters. No errors are swallowed.

items.name: Public API additions are additive and consistent across dialects
items.name_zh: 公共 API 新增保持向后兼容且各方言一致
items.evidence: Purely additive: an optional `windows?: [string, WindowSpec][]` field and an identical `.window()` method on pg, mysql, sqlite, gel and singlestore. The `${windowSql}` chunk is undefined when unused, so SQL for existing queries is unchanged. Exports go through `sql/expressions/index.ts`; no existing signature changed.
